title: Tracing Moral Foundations in Large Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating the internal encoding, organization, and expression of Moral Foundations Theory (MFT) dimensions using layer-wise activation projections, sparse autoencoders (SAEs), and causal steering interventions to measure shifts in moral judgments.

Comparing the internal geometric separability and structural representation of moral foundations between an English-centric model (Llama-3.1) and a Chinese-centric model (Qwen-2.5) to assess cross-cultural variability and WEIRD-centric value alignment.

Analyzing how Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) and safety fine-tuning structurally conflate and compress distinct compliance-oriented moral values (such as Fairness, Authority, and Loyalty) into a single dominant geometric cluster.
